claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy suitable for the proposed processing intervention.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 can produce an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure that retains composite lamellar features.
The tailored thermo-mechanical treatment specifically consists of controlled rolling followed by optimized annealing.
The as-cast baseline has a coarse or conventional eutectic microstructure lacking the refined duplex lamellar features.
The processed microstructure is an ultrafine-grained duplex structure with inherited lamellar composite features.
Phase decomposition in the processed alloy produces hierarchical structural heterogeneity.
The refined duplex microstructure generates a two-hierarchical constraint effect.
The two-hierarchical constraint effect helps distribute stresses during deformation.
The processed microstructure generates a microcrack-arresting mechanism.
The hierarchical constraint and microcrack-arresting mechanisms improve the alloy's mechanical response.
The processed material will have both higher strength and higher ductility than the as-cast material.
The strength improvement will be observable in yield strength and/or ultimate tensile strength.
The ductility improvement will be observable as increased elongation to failure.
Temperature, strain, and annealing time must be optimized to avoid overaging or grain coarsening.
Excessive annealing can cause grain growth and prevent the predicted strength-ductility improvement.
The predicted effect should extend to cast eutectic high-entropy alloys with compositions similar to AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The magnitude of the property improvement depends on processing parameters and small composition changes.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant simultaneous increase in strength and elongation relative to the as-cast control would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe the refined duplex lamellar structure would falsify the proposed intervention-to-microstructure relationship.
